newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea needs major economic policy changes - ADB.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea needs major economic policy changes - ADB.

text.p: South Korea must make major policy changes to adjust to a new relationship with the rest of the global economy, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Thursday.
"Although various measures have already been implemented, additional steps are required to achieve full financial and trade liberalisation," the ADB said in its annual outlook.
The outlook projects short-term economic trends in the region.
South Korea's membership in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development is expected to accelerate adoption of policies to restructure the economy, the bank outlook said.

To minimise short-term socio-economic costs of trade liberalisation, the ADB said the Korean economy needs greater flexibility in the labour market. The bank noted that government efforts to enact labour reforms have led to unrest.
Growth of South Korea's gross domestic product is expected to fall to 6.3 percent in 1997 from 7.0 percent last year, then recover to 6.9 percent in 1998, it said.
The bank attributed this year's decline to sluggish investments and a slowdown in exports.
The country's current account deficit should narrow to $18.5 billion in 1997 and $16.0 billion next year, from $23.7 billion in 1996, the ADB said.
South Korea's inflation rate should drop to 4.7 percent in 1997 and to 4.6 percent next year, compared to 5.0 percent in 1996, the outlook said.
